title: Kernel credentials are attribution evidence, not authorization
summary: The library exposes Linux SO_PEERCRED and SO_PASSCRED/SCM_CREDENTIALS so callers can obtain kernel-provided PID/UID/GID evidence, including credentials received with ancillary messages.
invariants: SO_PEERCRED and SCM_CREDENTIALS are kernel attribution evidence.
Kernel credentials do not themselves authorize an operation; application policy must decide what the attributed principal may do.
Credentials and SCM_RIGHTS may arrive in the same recvmsg result and remain separately represented.
Do not substitute caller-supplied identity strings for kernel credential evidence when the protocol relies on local peer attribution.
procedure: Enable passCredentials where per-message credentials are required and apply authorization after receipt.

provenance.claim: Security documentation classifies received rights, credential evidence, sendAll safety, and socket-option whitelisting.
